publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Formation of the interaction potential between two interacting atoms, molecules or nanoparticles is the well-known fact. Whereas the reason for attractive interaction is clear, appearance of the repulsive forces has not been studied in detail yet. It was shown earlier that repulsive forces occur for special system parameters or due to the nonlinearity of the nanoparticles properties. In the work we show theoretically that in system of two different-sized nanoparticles the repulsive interaction is formed due to the self-consistency of the system. The model exploits the quasi-point nanoparticles approximation, the Green function method for solving the Maxwell equations and the free energy expansion by the dipolar moment of the nanoparticle. Results of the work are important for understanding and further study of the near-field interaction at the nano-scale. As the model gives analytical result for the adsorption potential it is easy to use for analysis of experiments.

articleTitle: The Influence on the Conductive Interference Operation Mode of the Magnetic Core
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Inductors and transformers are an integral part of the Switched-mode Power Supply (SMPS), however the influence of the magnetic circuit of these components on the level of conductive interference was not considered. Approach to assessing the influence of the magnetic core parameters of inductors and transformers of SMPS on the level of electromagnetic interference (EMI) generated by the converter at different modes of operation of the inductor core is considered. By modeling it is shown that the level of conductive noise increases significantly when the core is operating on a nonlinear section of the characteristic.

articleTitle: The Stability of Single-Walled Carbon Nanotube: Lyapunov Function for Probe Needle
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: High mechanical strength and wear resistance determine the interest of using carbon nanotubes as probe needles. The analysis of the works has shown that on-line diagnostics of probe needles does not satisfy the development of nanoelectronics. The study of the stability of the probe needle and the creation of a model of its dynamic behavior in real time was conducted in the paper. In the presented paper the study of the behavior of AFM needle made of SWCNT is based on fundamental position of the notion of stability state of equilibrium of the needle as a physical system, introduced by A.M. Lyapunov.

articleTitle: Sensor Based on Diamond-Like Film Modified Electrodes for Bilirubin Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Traditional electrode materials used in electrochemical and electrochemiluminescent (ECL) water assays have a number of limitations. Among the promising solutions are electrode modification and new fabrication technologies of electrode materials. In this work, the results of the investigation of nanodiamond electrode material for electrochemical and electrochemiluminescent sensors are presented. A new kind of electrode material for electrochemical and electrochemiluminescent assays is nitrogen doped diamond-like films that are obtained using plasma vapor deposition process. The results of material properties study are very promising for applications of this material in different electrochemical analytical assays, for example, biomedical and ecological assays in water samples. Good behavior of nanodiamond electrode material in water assays allows obtaining high analytical characteristics of sensors based on the proposed material that was successfully tested for bilirubin detection.

articleTitle: Accuracy Increasing Approach in Aging-Aware Standard Cell Libraries
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The estimation of reliability of schemes has a great role at verification stage of integrated circuits. Estimation of reliability includes test of scheme considering circuit aging. As a result of aging the threshold voltage of transistors changes, which has a negative influence on digital integrated circuits concerning the growth of cells' delay. Therefore, the results of circuit aging should be considered in standard cell libraries.The influence of bias temperature instability and hot-carrier injection during aging of standard cells are researched in the article. Existing standard cells libraries, which are characterized considering the changes of duty-cycles of cells' input signals, are researched. It is shown that phase shift between input signals of a cell have great influence on cells' delay degradation during aging. A new approach of libraries characterization is proposed, in which phase shift between input signals of standard cells are considered, which increases the accuracy of measurement standard cells' delays more than 30 percent.

articleTitle: Design of Video Processing Platform with Interchangeable Input-Output Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The design and the prototype of a platform for video capturing and real-time processing are presented. Compared to other platforms, support of different input/output interfaces is achieved. Frame double synchronization is implemented by caching data in DDR2 memory leading to video transmission stability. Standard interfaces have been used between the main blocks to simplify the integration of image processing algorithms. The maximum input video resolution and usage of an external decoder for analog video inputs are the main limitations of the platform.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Algorithm for Detecting a Point Object on a Sequence of Video Images Using Decisive Statistics of Marks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Detection of point objects on a sequence of video images is an important step in optical monitoring systems for UAVs, since they allow them to be detected on the maximum range. This task is quite complicated because the intensity of the object in the image is low due to the low signal / noise ratio (SNR). Decisive statistics of marks are used to increase the effectiveness of object tracking. The paper presents a method for detecting point objects on a video images sequence according to Wald test using distributions of decisive statistics in likelihood ratio. Results of statistical modeling show that the synthesized algorithm reduces the detection time and reduce computational complexity compared with known algorithms detect a moving object IMM-PDAF-AI, which uses the decisive statistics of marks and IMM-PDAF, which does not use decisive statistics of marks.

articleTitle: SEM and Electrical Studies of Carbon Nanotube Reinforced PEDOT:PSS Layers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Nanocomposite layers of PEDOT:PSS polymer which incorporate randomly dispersed carbon nanotubes were thoroughly examined by means of high-resolution scanning electron microscopy and subjected to electrical studies at different frequencies in a wide range of temperatures. Comparison between the performance of pure PEDOT:PSS layers, layers reinforced with single-walled nanotubes and those reinforced with multi-walled nanotubes is made.

articleTitle: The Regression Parameters of Band Frequency Spectra of the Breath Sounds Vary in Course of a Respiratory Cycle
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Usually, the frequency content of the breath sounds is taken to be time-invariant and having the approximate decay of 12 dB per octave. This study deals with verification of this assumption by considering the short-time frequency spectra occurring in course of a respiration cycle. To approximate their shapes over the octave bands, a linear regression representation with respect to a logarithm of frequency is applied. The analysis of auscultation records shows the explicit time variation of linear regression parameters correlated with the respiratory activity. This property can be used as a marker in acoustic detection of the phases of a respiratory cycle.

articleTitle: Shadow Removal Algorithm for Remote Sensing Imagery
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This work is devoted to the problem of shadow removal from high-resolution remote sensing imagery. We investigated shadow properties in the HSV invariant color space. On the basis of the shadow properties we developed an enhanced algorithm that allows one to find paired shadow and non-shadowed regions of an image. The proposed algorithm shows better results than the previous one.

articleTitle: Low Power Design of XOR Circuit
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Anapproach of low power XOR gate is presented. Comparison has been done for traditional XOR and XOR heavysystems like binary to gray converter, parity checker. There are significant improvements in power consumption and area with cost of increaseddelay. As compared with traditional XOR gate this design consumes about 3 times less power and because of using less number of transistors area is decreased also. There is a disadvantage for this design in case of delay. It has about 30% more delay as compared with traditional XOR gate. Simulation was performed with SAED 32/28 nm technology.

articleTitle: Effects of Oxygen Content and Thermal Annealing on Sputtered a-IGZO Schottky Diodes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Effects of oxygen content during sputtering of amorphous In-Ga-Zn-O (a-IGZO) and post-deposition thermal annealing on the properties of vertical thin-film Schottky diodes were investigated. Increase of the oxygen content in the Ar/O2 mixture from 0 to 20% led to lower current densities. At the same time higher oxygen content enhanced the Ion/Ioff ratio of the Schottky diodes without post-treatment. The current-voltage characteristics exhibited a shift of the current minimum point depending on the bias sweep direction for the devices fabricated at 11.76% and 20% of oxygen. The post-deposition thermal annealing in air was found to improve the Ion/Ioff ratio with an optimum annealing temperature of 200°C although the effect depended on the initial oxygen content. Ideality factor and barrier height were calculated for all fabricated devices. Schottky diodes on glass based on IGZO sputtered at 3.23 - 6.25% of oxygen with Ion/Ioff ratio of 2.6·10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> - 1.6·10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> at ±1 V, ideality factor of 1.3 - 1.5, and barrier height of 0.62 - 0.67 eV were obtained after annealing at 200°C.

articleTitle: Software and Hardware Complex for Study of Photoelectric Properties of Semiconductor Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The method of measurement of electrical conductivity, photoconductivity and photomemory of semiconducting films, as well as electrical characteristics of photovoltaic cells of generators have been described. An electric circuit based on a 32-bit microcontroller is presented and a computer program is developed that provides automation of measurements, registration and initial processing of data, the possibility of constructing graphs of time and temperature dependencies for preliminary analysis of experimental data already in the process of measurement.

articleTitle: Physiological Reactions in Cereals Family Avena Sativa L. and Avena Nuda L., Caused by Low-Temperature Stress Factors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The cold stress leads to significant changes in physiological parameters, such as membranes permeability, the content of free proline and malonic dialdehyde (MDA), and violates the activity of the photosynthetic system. There is a significant oscillation in the manifestation of antioxidant system (AOS) components under the influence of lower temperatures: peroxidase (PER), superoxidedismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT). Have been showed that the content of proline and MDA in A. sativa increased significantly in comparison with the control plants; at the same time, the content of chlorophylls gradually decreased with increasing duration of stress factor in both studied species. It was determined that PER, SOD and CAT activity significantly increased under stress in A. nuda plants, which testifies to the higher adaptive threshold of this species.

articleTitle: Volatile Organic Compounds Detection by Metal-Assisted Etched Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In the paper, the possibility of volatile organic compounds detection by simple crystalline silicon - porous silicon structures obtained by metal-assisted chemical etching is studied. Obtained sensors demonstrate sensibility up to 5.8 A·cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/g. It is shown that depending on porous silicon formation process, samples can be selective to different organic compounds, possibly due to interaction of the analyte with surface electron states.

articleTitle: Differentiation of the 4D MRI Blood Flow Data to Estimate the Vorticity and Shear Stress in Aorta, Pulmonary Artery and the Heart
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) using three-dimensional velocity encoding phase contrast methods offers the opportunity to quantify time-resolved 3D flow patterns in vivo. This technique can have a breakthrough impact on the evaluation, risk stratification and surgical planning in hemodynamic-related pathologies, e.g., cardiac valve diseases, arterial stenos or insufficiency, dilation, dissection or coartaction. Nevertheless, the limited time and space resolution of 4D MRI data restricts the accuracy of derivative calculations, which are necessary for the estimation of some very important characteristics such as vorticity and shear stress in the blood flow. In this paper we introduce a new accuracy measure for the shear stress and calculate the possible discrepancy with the use of a new software tool which automatically segment the vessels and provides the information along the center line, between two selected cross-sections and in the vicinity of the selected points. Results are provided both as maximum and time-averaged values in aorta, pulmonary artery, left and right ventricles and valves. The cavitation phenomena, revealed in artificial mitral heart valves, cause interest in such studies for the real valves, especially for the patients suffering from different cardio-vascular diseases. To estimate possible cavitation inception the vorticity and pressure drop in mitral valve were estimated.

articleTitle: Ranking-based Placement of IC Logic Cells
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A method for placing logic cells of integrated circuits (IC) that takes into account the functional and logical features of the circuit. The proposed method is based on taking into account the flow of signals in the logic circuit. According to the proposed approach, a preliminary ranking of logical cells is performed, the results of which are later used in their placement. In accordance with the proposed method, an algorithm and software tool for allocation of logic ICs have been developed. Testing the program on test circuits showed the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Radiothermometric Measurements of Biological Objects Deep Temperature
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The new approach for measuring deep temperature of human body is proposed based on radio-thermometry. The novel design of radio-thermometer is developed and described containing microstrip antennas as an radio-thermometer applicator/receiver with significantly reduced coefficient of standing waves. The high efficiency of radio-thermometer is clinically proved for diagnostic of inflammatory processes in human body.

articleTitle: Ce-Doped Manganites of Lanthanum-Strontium as Promising Inducers of Magnetic Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Ce-doped nanoparticles of La-Sr manganite were synthesized via sol-gel method. Formation of the single-phased nanoparticles with the perovskite structure up to 5% of Ce was studied by X-ray diffraction method. Magnetic properties of obtained manganite nanoparticles were investigated. It was found that magnetic fluids based on the obtained nanoparticles heated up effectively under the action of an alternating magnetic field to 43-45°C.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach in the Fast Modelling of 2D Scattering From PEC Strip Using Nystrom Algortihm and the Beam Type Green’s Function
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The method of moments (MoM) procedure was combined with the complex source point (CSP) type Green's function to obtain faster solutions. Even though by this way, the cpu times are reduced drastically for large scatterers, the accuracy of this combination of MoM and CSP type Green's function is not better than the original MoM. On the other hand, here we performed a combination between Nystrom method and a special Green's function having a beam type radiation. Then it is expected to obtain more accurate data compare to MoM due to the convergent nature of Nystrom algorithm. It is also obtained the better running time performance than the original Nystrom method. Also this beam type of Green's function is derived from a general formulation of surface equivalence theorem and so the beam waist on the scatterer can be adjusted to a small value. The results are demonstrated on a single flat PEC strip and these statements are verified in the numerical results by comparing the RCS patterns. It is seen that the RCS patterns are very similar to original Nystrom case. Also the convergence of the results can be seen in the relative error plots for the total scattering cross section.

articleTitle: Computer Modeling of Human Thermoregulation for Electromagnetic Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Modeling prediction of human thermal state during effect of electromagnetic field (EMF) is the actual task. Preliminary model prognosis allows preventing human health hazard. This paper deals with the mathematical modeling of human thermoregulation during effect of radio frequency (RF) ranges. Information technology is based on the class of the mathematical dynamic models of human thermoregulation and allows simulating whole-body, regional and local hyperthermia. Modeling resulted in to conclusion that computer simulator can be effective approach for theoretical and practical tasks concerned with RF hyperthermia.

articleTitle: Size Effect in Multilayer Pyroactive Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Influence of size parameters on the frequency spectrum of the pyroelectric structures, as part of the sensitive element of pyroelectric detectors of radiation, is shown in this paper. This system is characterized by a pronounced dependence of the frequency spectrum of pyro-voltage on the ratio of films thickness are established. The obtained analytical results enable the development of recommendations for optimizing the performance of pyroelectric detectors of radiation based on multilayer sensitive elements.

articleTitle: Development High Sensitivity Sensors Based on Surface Plasmon Resonance Phenomenon
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Based on the analysis of known publications, the directions for enhancing the sensitivity of the sensor based on surface plasmon resonance are summarized. Additional porous Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> with optimal thinness 190 nm enable to take very large SPR-sensor response (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> effective refractive index change) that correspond to enhance of sensitivity in two orders. Porous SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> with optimal thinness 140 nm increase response of traditional 50 nm gold sensor by gas environment in more than 20 times, which provides an opportunity to detect the presence of harmful emissions in the atmosphere when they concentrate less than 1 mg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Functional coating increased sensitivity of SPR sensors in 15 times, that allow us to detect a lower concentration of antibodies in samples (1% of semi-positive serum, comparing to standard methods).

articleTitle: Simulation of the Sample Overheat for the Four Point Semiconductor Resistivity Measurement
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The results of the sample heating simulation by the measuring current when measured parameters of the semiconductor by the four-probe method are presented. The characteristics of the stationary heating mode are obtained and the introduced error is estimated. It is shown that for comparatively low-resistance samples with dimensions comparable to those of the probe, the effect of heating on the measurement error cannot be neglected. The transition process of heating in continuous and pulsed mode were investigated. The admissible heating levels for semiconductors of various conductivities are determined. The results obtained are new and useful for estimating errors in different resistivity measurement modes.

articleTitle: Morphology of Nanowire Arrays Produced by Metal-Assisted Chemical Etching on Si Wafers of Different Types: Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The results of studies on fabrication of silicon nanowires on the surface of silicon wafers of different types using the metal-assisted chemical etching method are presented. The influence of the deposition time of Ag particles on their morphology and filling density on the surface of silicon wafers has been analyzed. At different etching time of wafer samples of n-type in a HF-H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> based etching solution, vertically aligned arrays of solid nanowires are obtained. It is shown that changing the duration of Ag nanoparticles deposition at the same etching time, it is possible to change the distance between the nanowire stacks. It was established that under identical technological conditions the nanowires were not formed on a p-Si wafer. The results are discussed from the point of view of the specific etching mechanism of Si wafers with different type of conductivity and crystallographic orientation.

articleTitle: Microstructural Peculiarities Caused by Annealing in the Temperature-Sensitive Thick Films Based on Cu0.1Ni0.1Co1.6Mn1.2O4 Ceramics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Microstructural peculiarities in comparison with electrical properties in the temperature-sensitive thick films based on Cu0.1Ni0.1Co1.6Mn1.2O4 ceramics before and after annealing (ageing test at 170 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C for 500 h) are investigated. It is shown that annealing of thick films results in diffusion of Ag from contact area in region of grain boundaries. Obtained thick films with stabile electrical properties can be used as temperature-sensitive elements micro- and nanoelectronics.

articleTitle: Electrical Properties of Nanostructured MgAl2O4 Ceramics in Adsorption-Desorption Cycles
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Exploitative electrophysical properties of nanostructured MgAl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> ceramics sintered at maximal temperatures of 1100, 1200, 1300 and 1400 °C for 2 h and 1300 and 1400 °C for 5 and 9 h were studied at 50 °C and frequency of 500 Hz. Investigation in adsorption-desorption cycles were performed for MgAl2O4 ceramics after sintering, after ageing test at 40 °C and relative humidity of 95 % and after natural physical ageing in natural conditions (for ceramics sintered at 1200, 1300 and 1400 °C for 2 h). It is shown that ceramics prepared at 1100-1400 °C are slightly sensitive in the region of higher relative humidity. After ageing test these samples lose sensitivity in the region of low relative humidity. After ageing test humidity sensitivity of ceramics sintered at 1300 and 1400 °C for 2, 5 and 9 h are improved. Natural physical ageing results in slight changes in dependences of electrical resistance from relative humidity and narrowing of hysteresis of characteristics.

articleTitle: Cerium dioxide thin films in silicon MIS devices
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The article deals with the issues of replacing silicon dioxide in silicon MIS devices. The insulator choosing criterion for MIS structures based on certain semiconductor substrates is given. When using the insulator choosing criterion, cerium dioxide was chosen for use in silicon MIS structures. The results of the research of the MIS structure based on cerium dioxide are presented. Films of cerium dioxide were obtained by the oxidation of metal mirror and by the explosive evaporation methods. A comparison of MIS structures obtained using the both technological methods has been done. The expediency of replacing the silicon dioxide on the cerium dioxide in silicon MIS devices has been proved.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Interface Properties of Recombination Sensors From the Measurement of Capacitance-Voltage Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The problem of silicon substrate selection for the sensor structure based on deep junction barrier has been investigated. The described sensor is functioning on photoelectrical conversion principle for the illumination with has high absorption coefficient in the silicon. The method of substrate pre-selection with the measurement of capacitance-voltage characteristics has been suggested. As shape of the capacitance-voltage curves in the system liquid analyte/silicon substrate (with or without chemically modified silicon surface) highly depends on charge state of the interface and near-surface band bending, some recommendation for silicon substrate choosing can be used. The obtained results indicate that the shift of the saturation voltage of the capacitance-voltage curves correlates with peculiarities of photocurrent distribution in the deep silicon barrier structure. Based on the results of the research the effective recombination sensors with reproducible characteristics can be fabricated.

articleTitle: Simplyfied Universal Analytical Model for Defining of Plasma Boundary Position in the Glow Discharge Electron Guns for Forming Conic Hollow Electron Beam
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In the article the simplified analytical relations for estimation the plasma boundary position in the electrodes systems of high voltage glow discharge electron guns, formed the hollow conic electron beam, have been obtained. The distinguishing feature of proposed model is considering the main geometry parameters of simulated electrodes' system through the slope angle of anode surface. Analytical relation for defining position of plasma boundary relative to the cathode surface has been obtained by solving the cubic equation. The results of simulation for different slope angle of anode surface are presented and discussed.

Author Keywords: High Voltage Glow Discharge Electron Guns

articleTitle: High-Torque Piezomotor for Harsh Environments
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A high-torque, low-RPM special applications piezomotor was developed for harsh environment operations. The hollow internal channel of this special design allows accommodation for applications difficult for standard electromagnetic motors with gearboxes. Test results of a new design and perspective modification are presented.

articleTitle: A New Approach to Assessing the Perceived Contrast
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This paper is devoted to the problem of increasing the efficiency of no-reference assessment of the perceived contrast of images. The estimate of perceived contrast of the image is based on measuring the contrast of the image elements (objects) relative to each other. Contrast definitions for a pair of objects in an image are the basis for developing the no-reference metrics of image integral contrast. This paper proposes a new approach to quantify the perceived contrast for two objects in an image by assessing the contrast of these objects in a linearly-transformed (used as reference) image with a specified range of brightness values and subsequent normalizations of the obtained result of measurement. The range of brightness for the reference image are chosen in such a way as to provide an accurate measurement of the perceived contrast with using its definitions based on the Weber-Fechner law. Based on this approach a new generalized description of the perceived contrast of two objects in the image is presented. Proceeding from this description, new definitions of the weighted and relative contrast of a pair of objects in the image are proposed. Research results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach to quantify the perceived contrast of images.

articleTitle: Harmonic Balance Method and Convergence of the 2-D Nonlinear Eddy Current Problem
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A nonlinear model and the simulation method of the periodic magnetic field in a homogeneous conductive ferromagnetic medium is presented. The method is based on the simultaneous use of the harmonic balance method and the finite element method. The case of a magnetic field excitation by an alternating current source is considered. To solve the obtained system of the nonlinear equations the modified Newton's method was adopted. To accelerate the convergence of the iteration process the special optimization algorithm of a damping factor was used. The convergence of the algorithm is compared with COMSOL simulation. The convergence of harmonic balance finite element method is illustrated by samples with 3 odd harmonics. The resulting magnetic flux density of the presented approaches is compared too.

articleTitle: Nanostructures in the Formation of the Properties of High-Current Sliding Electrical Contacts on the Electric Rolling Stock
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The paper presents the results of bench tests of wear resistance of contact inserts of current collector runners made of "ROMANIT-UVLSh" material and their effect on the wear of the copper contact wire is evaluated. This material is a composite with a high content of electrically conductive lubricants capable of forming a thin conductive transition layer in a friction pair. Low temperature in the contact zone, indirectly, indicates a low transition resistance and high energy performance of the sliding contact, and low wear of the contact wire confirms its high tribological and mechanical properties. The use of contact inserts runner's current collectors made from this material is possible, both in alternating and direct current and can provide higher technical and economic indicators in comparison with traditional materials.

articleTitle: The Overshoot Reducing Method In Voltage Regulators In SAED 14nm FinFet Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This paper continues the main idea of previous research, where the fictive load was used to improve the overshoots in voltage regulators. The idea of this work is the decreasing of the existing voltage overshoot value in the regulators with 7 times by adding a digital-controlled fictive load as a compensation circuit to the actual load instead of the high-pass filter controlled load. The latter ensures more independent operation of the whole system on the process, voltage and temperature variations. Meanwhile compared with the previous method, this new scheme occupies about 4 times less area equal to 0.8um<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, of the integrated circuit.

articleTitle: Investigation of the ECG Leads Sensitivity to Myocardial Ischemia by Means of Biophysical Model
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A research of electrocardiogram leads sensitivity to changes in the shape of the transmembrane action potential curve, reflecting manifestation and development of myocardial ischemia was conducted. The research investigated different areas affected by ischemia and different scenarios of ischemia occurrence. The simulation indicated that changes occurred in ST-T interval were significantly higher than in both whole curve and QRS complex. However, sensitivity ratio of leads remained almost the same with small fluctuations. In all ischemia simulation scenarios sensitivity of precordial leads exceeded limb leads and augmented limb leads sensitivity (more than 63%). The most sensitive to simulated myocardial ischemia were four precordial leads V2 (12 %), V3 and V4 (about 14% in average each) and V5 (10 %), on ST-T interval and on the whole curve.

articleTitle: Subjective Assessment of the Influence of Room Characteristics on Intelligibility of Noised Speech
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A room is a special kind of filter that affects speech intelligibility in two ways. Late reverberation, like noise, reduces speech intelligibility, while early reflections increase speech intelligibility. The influence of the listening mode on the intelligibility of noised speech is also known. Binaural listening is preferable to monaural one because it allows increase intelligibility of speech distorted by noise and reverberation. In this paper, a subjective assessment of the influence of the lecture room characteristics on intelligibility of noised speech during binaural listening was made. The test stimuli were formed in two stages. First, white noise was added to the speech signal which had the form of consonant-vowel-consonant type monosyllable to provide the required signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in the range from minus 15 dB to plus 5 dB. Then the noisy speech was subjected to two-channel filtration using the binaural room impulse response (RIR) as the impulse response of the nonrecursive filter. Binaural RIRs measured for six different distances from the sound source (from 2.25 m to 10.2 m) in the lecture room of 10.8 × 10.9 × 3.15 m were used. Filtered phrases were listened through headphones, and monosyllables were identified and fixed by means of computer keyboard. The results of articulation tests showed that speech intelligibility is 7-10% higher for distances of 7-10 m than for a distance of 2.25 m with SNR = -10...-5 dB, which can be explained by the useful combined effect of early reflections and binaural listening. However, speech intelligibility for distances of 4-10 m turned out to be less than intelligibility for a distance of 2.25 m with SNR>3-5 dB, which can be explained by the prevalence of the detrimental effect of late reverberation over the action of noise at medium and large SNR values.

articleTitle: Controlling the Transport Defects of Power Generating Solar Panels
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Methodology for quality control of power generating panels is proposed. The methodology includes the two stages: detecting the defective power generating solar panels and controlling the influence of transport defects on the efficiency of power generating solar panels. There are specified procedures of preparing the recognition of transport defects, image preprocessing, recognition of transport defects and controlling the influence of panels detected on power capability.

articleTitle: Impedance Models of Double-Well and Three-Barrier Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Impedance models of double-well structure and three-barrier structure are developed and study of such structures characteristics are performed. Analytical expressions for double-well structure input impedance and eigenvalues are obtained. The dependence of double-well structure eigenvalues on the parameters of the structure is studied. The features of electrons resonant tunneling through a three-barrier structure are considered. Transmission coefficient characteristics of the three-barrier structure with different potential wells width are given. It is established that the coupling between three-barrier structure potential wells is capacitive in nature.

articleTitle: Influence of Various Factors on the Magnetite Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The paper shows the effectiveness of using contact non-equilibrium low-temperature plasma to produce magnetite.The effect of plasma synthesis parameters on the phase composition of the products was studied. The methods of X-ray phase analysis have established the effect of pH on the course of the process. Samples were obtained from precursor solutions having different pH values in the range of 7-12. Magnetic properties were studied using a vibration magnetometer. It is established that the dependence of magnetic characteristics on pH and processing time is nonlinear. The phase diagram has been constructed.

articleTitle: Investigation of the photodissociation quantum efficiency of hemoglobin derivatives
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The limit quantum efficiency of light interaction with oxyhemoglobin and carboxyhemoglobin at wavelengths of 525, 605 and 850 nm corresponding to the maxima of the action spectrum is studied. Obtained in vivo evaluations of the quantum yield of photodissociation of oxyhemoglobin HbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and carboxyhemoglobin HbCO range from 0.1 to 0.14 for HbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and from 0.76 to 0.90 for HbCO. The yield of photodissociation of carboxyhemoglobin is 6-8 times higher than that of oxyhemoglobin. Saturation of the processes of photodissociation is achieved with the same photon flux of approximately 11×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup> photons per second.The relatively low photodissociation quantum yield of oxyhemoglobin compaired to HbCO under conditions of in vivo experiment is hardly explain by geminate recombination or rebinding of ligands with heme, since irradiation was carried out continuously in contrast to experiments with time-resolved flash-photolysis which were used practically in all works devoted to the study of the kinetics of photodissociation of the ligand-heme complex and the determination of the quantum yield of the reaction. Most likely, the explanation of the relatively low quantum yield for HbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> should be explained by the protective properties of the structure of the oxyhemoglobin molecules and their environment in blood of a living organism.A significant difference in the quantum yields of photodissociation of oxy- and carboxyhemoglobin makes possible a selective forced decomposition of HbCO in blood with a minimal effect on HbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> component.

articleTitle: A Novel Voltage Mode High Speed Sense Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In applications with high voltage inputs traditional circuits of sense amplifiers can't achieve required speeds. An approach of stable Conventional Voltage Mode Sense Amplifier is presented. Both existing and new approaches have been used to fix the issue. Compared to traditional circuit CLK2Q delay has been decreased by almost 25% with power consumption increasing by 20,5%. Area was also increased during the modifications. Improvements are seen in robustness against on chip variation. Proposed circuit was simulated using SAED 14nm Finfet technology and showed much better results not only for standard 3 sigma range but also in 5 sigma range covering almost all possible scenarios.

articleTitle: A Reconstruction Approach for Non-contract Photoacoustic Tomography
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Noncontact holographic photoacoustic tomography (PAT) is a new noncontact imaging method where tissue displacement is used for a primary pressure absorber reconstruction. The imaging method has the same physical fundamentals as contact PAT imaging, therefore for noncontact PAT reconstruction may be used known reconstruction procedure of contact PAT. It is only necessary to develop an approach of recalculation the displacement on tissue border to pressure. The recalculation approach proposed in the paper is based on the momentum conservation law. A model for the approach implemented in the k-Wave toolbox. A high quality of experimental data reconstruction confirms the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Magnetization Dynamics Mediated by a Heating Pulse in Nanoscale Magnetic Element
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: We analyze magnetization dynamics in a nanoscale magnetic element (e.g. magnetic nanodot) under the action of a thermal heating pulse that rapidly increases the temperature of the system for a short period of time. Using macrospin approximation we calculate the magnetization dynamics in the system and reveal the pulse-stimulated excitation of a quasi-uniform magnetization mode that can also indicate the presence of the Bose-Einstein condensation process in the considered system.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Processes in Serial-To-Parallel Resonant Converter for Contactless Charging of Electric Vehicle Battery
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The electromagnetic processes in the power section of the serial-to-parallel resonant converter for contactless charging of electric vehicle battery are analyzed. The solutions of the vector-matrix equations, which describe the processes in the power section of the resonant converter for contactless inductive charging have been obtained with the usage of the state-variable method, which allow to obtain the dependence of the average value of the output current on the parameters of the circuit elements, load and the length of the transformer gap. The load and control characteristics of the converter are obtained and analyzed.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Non-Enzymatic Detection of Glucose at Nanostructured Multilayer Electrode
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Multilayer coating consisting of alternating nanoscale layers of nickel-copper alloy and a mixture of metals with hydroxides were obtained by electrodeposition on copper wire from polyligand pyrophosphate-ammonia electrolyte by two-pulse potentiostatic method. Cyclic voltammetry study shows that the electrode demonstrate catalytic activity in reaction of glucose oxidation at the potentials of Ni(OH)2/NiOOH redox transition. The electrode can be used for non-enzymatic glucose detection. Sensitivity of electrode in 0.1 M KOH with 1-50 μA glucose is 13986±9 μA mM<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> at +0.54 V and 1667±4 μA mM<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> for up to 6.3 mM glucose concentration at +0.6 V.

articleTitle: Some Advantages of Silicon Nanowires for Photovoltaics Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The silicon nanowires have large prospects for various applications in electronics and optoelectronics. One of them is the Si nanowire based solar cells with radial p-n junction. The results on theoretical and experimental investigations on influence of the silicon nanowires parameters on short circuit current in structures with radial p-n junction are presented. The experimentally obtained value of shortcircuit current is higher in comparison with the theoretical one for determined nanowires parameters. The possible explanation of this fact is given.

articleTitle: Preparation of CdхMn1-хTe Crystal Surface by Laser Irradiation for Formation of Barrier Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The transformations of the morphology and surface structure of Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Te crystals under the action of pulsed laser radiation and the properties of laser-optimized barrier structures on these crystals obtained by high-frequency cathode sputtering were studied. Using scanning electron (SEM) and atomic force (AFM) microscopy, it was shown that, depending on the energy density and laser pulse duration, the morphology, phase composition and distribution of the system of defects and inclusions in the surface areas of Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Te crystals can be optimized. A theoretical prediction of the surface temperature and the melting threshold of Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Te crystals for various laser treatment modes was made. It was shown that the quality of the laser treated surface Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Te crystals (x=0.1-0.45) can be estimated from the maximum contrast of the lines in the electron channeling patterns in SEM. Active heterostructures were obtained using the RF cathode sputtering of thin CdSb, ZnSb films Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Te crystals. The transformation of the polycrystalline granular structure of these films in the field of the laser action was studied using scanning images in AFM. It was found that grains coalescence processes contribute to the optimization of both the adhesion and structure of the films, as well as the electrophysical characteristics of the barrier structures.

articleTitle: Remote Study of the Earth Stratospheric Aerosol
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Changes in the Earth's climate are mainly caused by disruptions in the energy balance of the Sun-Earth system. This process is the result of natural changes and the influence of anthropogenic factors. Their cumulative effect leads to a decrease in the thickness of the ozone layer, the global warming and other cataclysms on the planet. To study of the stratospheric aerosol the Main Astronomical Observatory of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine proposed to conduct a satellite polarimetric experiment in the ultraviolet (UV) spectrum range to obtain information on the physical properties of the aerosol for the results of polarimetric and photometric sky measurements. MAO NAS of Ukraine, the National Technical University of Ukraine "KPI" and L'viv Polytechnic National University have developed and created a miniature UV polarimeter (UVP). The proposed method allows to cut off the influence of the tropospheric component of the atmosphere and the Earth's surface and to select for the study only the polarization component of the stratospheric aerosol. To carry out ground-based polarization observations of a cloudless sky a modification of previous model of UVP were carried out on the AZT-2 telescope in the Main Astronomical Observatory. That is, even such an approximate analysis of ground-based polarization observations of a cloudless sky during the day and after sunset make it possible to study the physical characteristics of the aerosol in the troposphere and stratosphere.

articleTitle: University Nanosatellite Television Camera
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In recent years, there is a strong tendency to reduce the size of orbital spacecrafts while preserving their functional capabilities. The modern element base allows to create inexpensive Earth-sensing satellites having the 1U-2U form factor, which is capable to form images of the Earth’s surface with medium spatial resolution. In order to perform synthesis of such optoelectronic remote sensing equipment, a relatively simple calculation technique is required. In this research, a technique has been developed to analyze an information system "Earth’s surface – atmosphere – television camera". It allows to determine the basic parameters of a lens and a matrix detector of the television camera, based on harmonization of their resolution and providing a given spatial resolution on the surface of the Earth.By using the proposed technique, a lens and a matrix detector have been selected. They provide the geometric resolution of 25 m at the orbit with a height of 600 km.

articleTitle: Microstrip Composite Structures with Electromechanical Control
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In this article, controlled microwave structures based on composite microstrip lines are considered. A simple method of calculating such structures adapted to the engineering needs is presented. The results of numerical verification of the proposed methodology are presented. Practical designs of a microwave filter and a phase shifter with electromechanical control based on composite microstrip lines are shown.

articleTitle: Mobility of Polarons in Semiconductors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The polaron mobility of a semiconductor is studied on the basis of kinetic equation for polaron subsystem interacting with equilibrium phonon subsystem in the presence of small external electric field. The mobility is discussed with a connection to polaron subsystem velocity relaxation. Relaxation processes in the system are studied on the basis of spectral theory of the collision integral operator in the presence of the electric field. Contribution of the electric field to the velocity relaxation time equation is found in the simplex approximation comparing this equation with the Newton second law. The basic equations of the theory are solved by the method of truncated expansion in the Sonine polynomial series. The velocity relaxation coefficient and mobility of polaron are calculated in one-polynomial approximation. It is established that the nonequilibrium polaron distribution function differs from the Maxwell distribution with polaron velocity and temperature. Relation of the developed theory with the Bogolyubov method of the reduced description of nonequilibrium systems is discussed. For semiconductors of the groups A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">III</sup>B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">V</sup> velocity relaxation coefficient and mobility are found numerically.

articleTitle: New in the Theory of Periodic Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: New results in the theory of periodic structures (PSs), obtained on the basis of stepped transmission line model, are presented. It is shown that PSs peculiarly transform the wave impedance, inducing unusual properties of the wave medium. Stepped transmission line model makes it possible to determine the fundamental relationships of physics and mathematics for PSs. Model of impedance delta-inhomogeneities allows to get simple analytical expressions for PS characteristics. Two-phase PSs for which band gap frequencies are twice lower than those for traditional single-phase PSs are considered.

articleTitle: Directivities and Thresholds of Laser Modes of Triangular Active Microcavities with Piercing Holes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Directivities, spectra, and thresholds of laser modes of an equilateral triangular active microcavity with a piercing hole are calculated numerically solving the Lasing Eigenvalue Problem on the basis of the set of Muller boundary integral equations. An effective Nyström approximation is used. The computational experiments demonstrate that a hole located at certain place and having suitable radius can lead to a notable growth of the directivity of the lasing emission with the conservation of the low thresholds.

articleTitle: Formation of Hard Magnetic FePt Based Films on Amorphous Silicon Oxide and Sapphire Substrates by RTA
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Ordering and structural transformations as well as the magnetic properties of the ordered tetragonal FePt phase formed by rapid thermal annealing (RTA) of the Pt/Fe layered stacks on amorphous silicon oxide and sapphire substrates were investigated. It is shown that a higher level of compressive stresses in the Pt/Fe layered films on the silicon oxide substrate promotes the ordering process, improves magnetic properties of the films and leads to a higher number of grains oriented in the [001] direction perpendicular to the film plane.

articleTitle: Phase Shift Consideration Mechanisms in Aging-Aware Standard Cell Libraries
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Aging-aware standard cell libraries are characterized to estimate aging impact on digital integrated circuits (IC) and to measure parameters of digital IC after degradation. In existing libraries cells are characterized considering cell's input signals' slops, output loads and input signals' duty cycles. However, besides duty cycle, aging has different impacts on cells depending on the phase shift between input signals. Standard cells' input signals phase shift sweeping mechanisms are proposed in this paper during characterization of standard cell libraries, which have high accuracy and don't require huge machine resources and simulation run time.

articleTitle: Deformation-induced Magnetoconductance in Silicon Whiskers near Metal-insulator Transition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Silicon whiskers with boron concentration 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> were chosen to investigate magnetoconductance in the range 0-14 T at 4.2 K under compressive deformation up to -2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> rel.un. Deformation influence on spin-orbital splitting on the valence band spectrum was studied. As result, the splitting of light and heavy hole branches was found under compressive deformation according to kp-method. The spin splitting energy Δ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">so</sub> was found due to studying the longitudinal magnetoconductance of Si whiskers at 4.2 K.

articleTitle: The Effect of Proton Irradiation on the Resistance of Gold Contacts on Silicon
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The sample for the experimental studies was the layered metal-semiconductor formation. There have been the two films of gold of 50 nm thicknesses deposited unto opposite surfaces of p-silicon with a surface layer of silicon oxide. The effect of 1.5 MeV proton beam on sample was investigated. Only the uncovered by films surface of the sample was irradiated. The integral dose of irradiation was 2*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> p / cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The direction of the proton beam was parallel to the contacts. Performed with the irradiated sample experiments detected changes of the electrical properties of the gold film contacts far away from the active region of irradiation. After irradiation the contact resistance decreased by several times.

articleTitle: Effect of Sparse Doping in Barriers on the Energy Structure of Center-Delta-Doped QW
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Effect of sparse (presumably background) shallow donor impurity on the energy structure of SiGe/Si quantum well structure delta-doped to the center of the well is studied numerically. The method includes calculation of impurity binding energy. The proposed nanostructure configuration can be used to create tunable optical devices in THz frequency region.

articleTitle: Modeling Conductance Cutoff of GaN, AlN and InN at High-frequency Region
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: At the article new approach of cutoff estimation by Fourier spectrum pulse response at high-frequency region with an approximation for drift speed of III-Nitride semiconductor materials - (Al, In, Ga)N is investigated. The frequency-domain limits of negative dynamic conductance are compared with resulting cutoff frequencies for III-Nitrides. The advantage of III-Nitrides in terms of frequency characteristics and features of each of the representatives of the group are demonstrated. From a methodological point of view proposed approach is based on the solving of the differential equation system. System consists of relaxation expressions for energy, impulse and carrier concentration. For various types of scattering are taken into account specific relaxation times.

articleTitle: Capacitive and Inductive Properties of Composite Films with Silicon and Metal Nanocrystals
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The results on investigations of the impedance of the oxide based nanocomposite films containing silicon and metal nanocrystals are presented. The voltage and frequency dependences of the capacitive and inductive parts of the impedance of structures with SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>(Si, Fe) and SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>(Si, Al) films are analyzed in detail. It was established the the power dependence on the frequency according to the Mott's law for the hopping transport on alternating current. As it was revealed in the structures with nanocomposite SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>(Si, Al) film the capacitive component dominates in the reactive part of the impedance. On the other hand in the structure with nanocomposite SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>(Si, Fe) film the reactive component of the impedance has an inductive character up to the frequency of 1 MHz. The obtained results point out on the possibility to use the SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>(Si, Fe) film as the flat film inductance in the HF micro- and nanoelectronics circuits.

articleTitle: A 13.56 MHz RF Frontend with Current-Mode Demodulator for Wide Input-Power Dynamic-Range
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This article presents the design of an analog RF frontend for a 13.56 MHz transponder which can operate in a wide range of input powers. The frontend allows wireless telemetric data transmission and also powers the whole system. Implemented in a 0.35 μm CMOS technology the design includes the full-wave rectifier with voltage limiter, low dropout regulators with bandgap reference, a current-mode ASK demodulator supporting modulation indices from 10 to 40 %, clock recovery circuit, and a digital protocol engine. The modulator and demodulator allow the application in ISO 18003 Mode 1 compliant systems. The incident power can range from 460 μW up to 460mW and resistive loads up to 1 kΩ can be applied. The current consumption of the analog frontend itself is only 150 μA and it occupies an area of 0.85 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in the chosen CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Modeling of ECG and creation artificial database with synthetic T-wave alternans
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This paper presents the electrocardiogram (ECG) modeling approach with different level of T-wave alternans (TWA). To create a variety of signals, 17 parameters were used, where three parameters were changed to create a signal with different level and types of the T-wave alternans. Type of T-wave alternans depended on: T-wave amplitude, duration of Q-T interval, T-wave amplitude and the duration of Q-T intervals. Generation of the alternans parameters were carried out with constant and varied HR. Parameter root mean square value of difference odd and even T-waves (rmsTmean) was chosen for the analysis of the influence of different level of the T-wave alternans on a synthetic ECG. A change in heart rate adds an additional error in determining the level of alternation ECG, which may not be related to the T-wave alternans.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Oscillator on Surface Acoustic Waves Adapted to Frequency Regulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This article presents the results of a study of the improved structure of a oscillator on surface acoustic waves with dynamic electronic control of frequency. The structure and principle of operation of the oscillator are presented, which allows increasing the frequency adjustment band. It is shown that to increase the working frequency range it is necessary to simultaneously form an optoelectronic method using both an input and an output counter-to-pin converter.

articleTitle: Preparation and Characterization of One-Layered Humidity-Sensitive Thick Films for Sensor Electronics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Humidity-sensitive one-layered thick films based on MgAl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> ceramics were prepared. Electrophysical properties (dependence of electrical resistance on relative humidity) were investigated before and after degradation cycle at 40 °C at 95 % of relative humidity. Thick films are sensitive in the region from 55 to 99 % of relative humidity. It is established that poor humidity-sensitivity in the region of low values of relative humidity are connected with imperfect porous structures in the region thick films - contact area.

articleTitle: Sillenites as Dielectric Materials with Low Microwave Absorption
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Sillenites combine the properties, important for microwave microelectronics, possessing at the same time: (1) high piezoelectric module, which provides piezoelectric resonance, (2) high dielectric constant, necessary for obtaining dielectric resonators, and (3) low acoustic and dielectric losses, guaranteeing high quality of both resonances. The paper contains detailed studies of sillenites of different composition and different degrees of doping at frequencies of 10 GHz in order to assess their potential for use as components of metamaterials.

articleTitle: Reflectivity of Porous Silicon Matrix as Analyte ‘Logical’ Pattern
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The reflectivity of porous silicon single layer optical sensor was calculated by matrix method for different values of porosity and porous layer thickness. Parameters of interferences peaks were determined for sensors with pores filled with liquid analytes. Dependence of peak parameters on porosity, layer thickness and wavelength is considered as a pattern of the analyte. Method of decreasing dimension of response matrix was proposed. The reflectivity of filled with analyte end unfilled pores at specific points considered as "logical" state of analyte pattern.

articleTitle: Passive Method for Raman Gain Measurement Using Backward Pumped Fiber Configuration
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The passive measurement method for the Raman gain profile in singlemode fiber is presented in this work. Experimental technique is worked out for the standard fibers based on silica glass. The optical power density of amplified spontaneous emission for Stokes shifted region up to 1600 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> was measured in the 50 km fiber span. The main advantage of the proposed method consists in the absence of external signals of variable frequency as it is used the measurement of amplified spontaneous emission in the idle mode of counter-pumped fiber Raman amplifier.

articleTitle: Flotation Process Optimization Using High-Energy Ultrasound Frequency Control
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The paper describes a method, which allows controlling the composition of iron ore pulp solid and gas phases and forming the desired gas bubble size distribution function, which corresponds to the pulp solid particle size distribution in the flotation process using high-energy ultrasound of a given frequency. To form an automatic control of the ultrasound exposure frequency, the algorithm, which automatically corrects the combinations of the output frequencies of the inverter voltage depending on the direction of the effective values of the current and the frequency of the output voltage is used. This allows adjusting the voltage-controlled oscillator to the resonant frequency of the converter. The control system is based on measuring the effective value of the current of the voltage generator, which is tuning the frequency of the voltage-controlled oscillator, which is generating a rectangular voltage wave with a fixed maximum value, which displays the output voltage of the inverter. To simplify the calculations, an adaptive fuzzy controller was used in the model of the digital frequency control system.

articleTitle: Polarimetric Technologies for Object`s Attitude Sensing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The paper deal with researching the possibility of applying polarimetric technologies for increasing the sensitivity and accuracy of object's attitude sensing. The article considers the existing methods for determining the object`s attitude sensing and systems that implement them. In addition, the polarimetric principle of determining the direction to the source of polarized radiation and the device that implements it is proposed in the article. The article presents the results of the mathematical modeling of proposed system's work.

articleTitle: Uniform Dielectric Cylinder with a Graphene Coating as a Lens
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: We investigated the focusing effects arising in the diffraction of H-polarized plane wave by a uniform dielectric cylinder with a graphene coating. The analytical solution of the wave-scattering problem is based on the Maxwell equations and the resistive boundary conditions on the zero-thickness graphene cover where the graphene electron conductivity was determined from the Kubo formalism. We use the spectra of normalized cross-sections: scattering and the absorption for finding the frequencies of plasmon resonance in graphene layer. Spatial distribution was computed of the field amplitude in the absorption maxima. Computations were performed out in the wide range of cylinder radius and the wavelength of incident radiation. We demonstrate that the field focusing at the rear surface of the cylinder takes place when the surface plasmon resonance occurs in the structure; the resonance frequencies of different plasmon modes fall into a wide band. An optimal value of the cylinder radius and the frequency of the incident wave were found corresponding to the highest focusing effect.

articleTitle: Fiber Bragg Grating Cavities in Two-Wave Raman Laser for Terahertz Telecommunication Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: All-fiber original design of the two-wave (2λ) fiber Raman laser (FRL) is suggested for terahertz telecommunication application. It is shown, that the Raman gain profile in single mode fibers allows realizing the 2λ FRL. It is intended for operation in full range up to 10 THz with proper formation lasing cavities using the fiber Bragg gratings. Modeling results on parameters of laser resonators built on fiber Bragg gratings are presented for three actual terahertz bands. Advantages of the 2λ FRL based on the Raman fiber (silica fiber doped 20 % GeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) are analyzed in more detail in comparison with the ordinary pure silica fiber recently used for other FRL application. The creation possibility of 2λ FRL as an important part of future telecommunication systems of the terahertz range is demonstrated and it is proved by simulation.

articleTitle: Structure, Morphology and Spectroscopy Characterization of the Lа1-X-YErx/2Eux/2CayVO4 Sol-Gel Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The lanthanum vanadate nanoparticles doped with europium and erbium ions and co-doped with calcium ions were prepared by aqueous nitrate-citrate sol-gel synthesis route taking citric acid as a complexing agent. Phase composition, crystal lattice parameters and microstructure of the synthesized samples were established using various methods. The XRD analysis has revealed dependence of crystal structure on dopants concentration: monoclinic monazite-type structure for low dopant concentrations and tetragonal zircon-type structure for high dopant concentrations. The photoluminescence emission spectra are presented by narrow lines caused by f-f transitions in the rare earth activators. The relations between crystal phase structures and luminescence properties were discussed.

articleTitle: Resonance Excitation Conditions of the Luminescence in the Layered Structure with a Gain Layer
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Resonance excitation conditions of a luminescence in a prism-based structure consisting dielectric layer with low refractive index and layer of luminophor with high refractive index have been determined using matrix method. The influence of the refractive indices of the dielectric layers and their thickness on the wavelength at which the resonance mode is excited has been studied.

articleTitle: Supplements to Invertor Current Mode Controller of Distributed Generation Sources for Stability Task
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Impact of distributed generation on power systems has caused considerable recent research interest. Development of distributed generation sources, usually uses renewable energy, associate with power electronics in field of development invertors. Consequently, much research in recent years has focused on improving invertors and their control systems. Actual task is to forming information and control signals for invertor current mode controller, according to results of stability evaluation algorithm. This algorithm aimed on provides stable operation of power system. In addition, it should be proposed supplements to logic of current mode controller into invertor. Our results focus on improving of invertor performance, consist of control systems dexterity extension. Results are propose procedure of creating control signals, aimed on provide stable operation of electrical network. Suggestions on development module of stability estimation and forming control signals are made. Our results have potential on dexterity extension of current mode controller operation, therefore, total performance of invertor.

articleTitle: Morphology and Functional Properties of Magnetic Nanoparticles of Lanthanum-Strontium Manganites
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 39th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Structure, morphology, magnetic state and magnetocaloric effect of single-phase nanopowder La<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</sub>Sr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</sub>MnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> manganites have been investigated by X-ray diffraction, BET, SEM, and magnetic methods. According to X-ray diffraction, BET and SEM data, an average size of particles for the La<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</sub>Sr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</sub>MnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> composition is tens of nanometers. On the basis of analysis of the magnetic data, the magnetic states, phase transition temperatures, magnetocaloric effect as well as critical sizes of particles, i.e. boundary sizes of a single-domain state, a vortex state and a multi-domain state, have been determined. The most part of nanoparticles of the La<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</sub>Sr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</sub>MnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> composition are in the single-domain state.

articleTitle: Top-down Synthesized CdSe Nanoparticles for Electroanalytical and Labeling Applications
